muestra.texto:
**Ask ProDeck** is a box at the top of **No sound?** (phone: Home → No sound?; booth: Routing → No sound?). Type what is wrong in your own words — "Ruth's mic is crackling", "nothing from the keys", "the stream is quiet" — and it answers the way an experienced tech would: one clarifying question if it needs one, what ProDeck already checked, then the next thing to walk to and look at.

It can only say what this building's **routing map**, **knowledge files** and **live state** say. Every fact it uses is tied to a thing on the map, shown as a link under the answer — tap it to open the walk. It never touches the desk.

To turn it on: **Settings → Troubleshooter**, paste an Anthropic API key (console.anthropic.com), pick a model, and choose whether crew phones may ask. The key stays on the booth; phones ask through it.

- **Knowledge files.** A folder on the booth (Settings shows where) holding plain markdown about your building: machines and addresses, which scenes are safe to recall mid-service, what feeds what, known oddities. Everything in it is read on every question. Write what a new sound tech would need.
- **The log.** Every question and answer is kept on the booth so whoever owns the room can see what was asked and fix the notes.
- **The cap.** A monthly call limit, 500 by default, so a stuck phone can't run up a bill.

> Its general sound knowledge is a written method that ships with ProDeck — signal-flow reasoning, symptoms and causes, wireless, Dante, scenes, rules during a service. It is told to reason from that text and this building's notes, not from memory.

muestra.texto:
Every booth has a **crew address**, **https://yourname-crew.prodeck.live**. It's on unless you turn it off in **Settings → Crew & screens → Crew address**, and there's nothing to set up: no port forwarding, no domain, no tunnel.

**With ProDeck open at the booth,** crew open the crew address from home or on cellular and get the live booth, the same as on the church Wi-Fi. The booth keeps one connection out to White Oak Media's service, and phones' requests come to it that way. Passwords and permissions are checked by the booth, as always. Comms, camera feeds and the overflow audio stay on the church Wi-Fi.

**With the booth computer off,** the crew address shows the last copy the booth sent: this week's plan (songs, keys, leaders, times, who's on, call times and position guides), checklists and team chat. A line at the top says so plainly, with the time it was sent. Checklist ticks, chat messages and signups made then wait there and reach the booth when it's back.

Crew links, the poster and QR codes don't change. A phone that can't reach the booth on its usual address reads the copy from the crew address by itself, and moves over to it when the booth is on but out of reach (the phone left the building), keeping its sign in. ProDeck Crew does the same.

The name is your secure local address's name if you claimed one, else one made from this computer's name (change it in the card). What the copy holds and who keeps it is in **Settings → About → Privacy**. Turning the crew address off deletes the copy.

muestra.texto:
Honest summary, so you can decide what to expose:

- **Two shared passwords** decide what a phone may do. Anyone with the crew password is crew. Choose long ones; rotate the crew password if a phone is lost (it signs everyone out — send the new join link).
- **Crew PINs are four digits.** They identify people, they don't protect anything; the passwords do. Wrong PINs lock the name for five minutes.
- **Joining needs you.** Outside a joining window you open, the poster only lets someone ask to join; nobody gets in until you approve them.
- **The web gateway throttles password guessing** and refuses requests from other websites.
- **Secrets never leave the booth in the clear**: phones receive settings with every password and key removed; the diagnostics bundle is scrubbed before it's copied.
- **A kiosk bookmark holds the crew password** and can be read off that machine. Don't put the admin password in one.

- **Grants are per person and revocable.** Giving someone Page or Control doesn't hand them the admin password, and revoking their approval removes every grant at once.

Security problems: **SECURITY.md** in the repository explains how to report privately.

muestra.texto:
Comms turns crew phones and iPads into a hold to talk intercom. It's **off until you turn it on** in **Settings → Crew & screens → Comms**; leave it off if your team already has an intercom, and it appears nowhere. On a phone: **More → Comms → Join comms**, allow the microphone, pick the line to talk on, and hold the big button while you speak. There are four lines: **All**, **Cameras**, **Stage** and **Booth**. Choose which ones you listen to; everyone hears All unless they turn it off. A chip at the top of every screen shows who's talking and has its own **Talk** button. For hands-free comms, turn on **Open mic**: you talk without holding anything until you turn it off, and the big button (and the chip's) becomes **Mute** and **Unmute**. Open mic always starts muted when you join, so a mic never opens by itself.

Phones talk straight to each other over the church Wi-Fi, so the delay is a fraction of a second. ProDeck only connects them, and the booth computer never plays comms: it can't reach the house.

What it needs:

- **A secure address.** Phones only allow the microphone on https. Claim a **secure local address** in Settings (it takes a minute, nothing to set up), or use your own public address. On the plain local address, Join comms explains this instead of starting.
- **Phones on the church Wi-Fi.** A phone on cellular still joins (the public address reaches the booth from anywhere), but it can't reach the other phones, so nobody hears it. A guest network that keeps devices apart does the same. Use the staff network. **On comms** says **can't reach** next to anyone this happens with.
- **The app open, screen on.** A locked iPhone stops a web app's sound and microphone. Comms suits people at a post with the phone in view, like a camera operator using the phone as a tally. Use earbuds so the phone's speaker doesn't feed back into its mic.

**Camera stations.** An iPad that lives on a camera doesn't need anyone's account. Make its code in **Settings → Camera tally**, scan it on the iPad, add it to the Home Screen, and tap the tally once to **Join comms**. It shows up on comms under the camera's name, with Talk or Mute in the corner and Open mic in the tap menu, and rejoins by itself (muted) whenever it reopens. Plug a headset into it, set Auto-Lock to Never, and use Guided Access to keep it on the tally.

A device that was on comms rejoins by itself when it reopens. If the phone wants a tap before it hands over the microphone, it shows **Tap to rejoin comms**. **Leave comms** stops that until you join again.

Up to 16 devices can be on comms at once.
